title: AI account reconciliation: will it speed our close and pass audit?
description: What AI really does in reconciliations, which of 15 tools publish prices, what auditors expect, and three builds for a 40-500 person finance team.
verdict: AI clears the matches it is sure of and queues the rest for a person[^3][^4].
Fix review controls first, because late reconciliation review already causes material weaknesses[^8][^7].
Your auditor will test who reviews and signs, and whether the data behind each match is reliable[^13][^12].
Close platforms don't list prices; quotes scale with transactions, seats or close scope[^28][^30].
On QuickBooks or Xero with one entity, try the built-in AI reconcile first[^6][^37].

headings.what-it-is: What does AI actually do in a reconciliation?
headings.human-role: Who still reviews and signs off?
headings.buy-or-build: Should you buy a close platform or use what you have?

summary: Account reconciliation compares two sets of records, such as your ledger and a bank statement, and explains each difference[^1]. AI suggests matches with a confidence level and leaves the unsure ones for a person[^3][^4]. Controls make or break it: late reconciliation review already shows up in material weakness reports[^8].
humanRole: A staff accountant prepares each reconciliation and a different person reviews it, and both sign every month[^2][^1]. The reviewer checks the support behind it, not just the final balance[^2][^1].
The controller approves reconciliations on time. The SEC has cited late review as a control deficiency, and public companies report it as a material weakness, a serious control gap[^7][^8].
Keep duties split, so no one person controls every step or can override the automated matching[^1]. Whoever sets the AI's matching rules and thresholds should not also approve the reconciliation[^1].
Auditors still reach their own conclusions, and AICPA guidance flags made-up answers and unexplainable output as AI risks[^9][^10]. Treat AI-written explanations as drafts a person checks[^9].
teamAfter: The preparer works the exceptions. Xero posts only the matches it is sure of, and Workday suggests matches for a person to accept[^4][^3].
Preparers accept or reject each AI suggestion and check each AI-written explanation before the reviewer sees it[^3][^9].
Most finance teams already use AI somewhere: 59% in Gartner's 2025 survey, with error and anomaly detection a top use[^19]. Fewer than half say they can show auditors how their AI works[^20].

ownData.title: Which reconciliation tools publish a price? We checked 15 pages
ownData.intro: We checked 15 vendor pricing pages on 26 Nov 2026 for a published price and a named AI feature[^27][^37]. Five of the 15 publish a price. None of the eight dedicated close and reconciliation platforms do[^27][^29][^34].
rows: AI matching, variance explanations, anomaly routing[^27]
Cash matching of "up to 95%" of bank lines (vendor claim)[^28]
One fee by close scope, not per user[^30]
Agentic close, AI variance analysis (explains month-to-month swings), continuous reconciliation[^30]
$250 per named user a month, 10-user minimum[^23]
AI-powered reconciliation on Plus and up[^38][^6]
AI bookkeeping and reconciliation on all plans[^39]
ownData.note: Method: we fetched each vendor's own pricing page, or its product page where none exists, on 26 Nov 2026. Some fetches returned cached copies, dated 13 Nov 2025 to 25 Nov 2026, as noted in the sources. List prices are not what firms pay, and ERP add-ons bundle other modules.

example.input: Illustrative. A month's bank statement as CSV or PDF, the ledger's cash detail, a card processor's payout report, open customer invoices and remittance emails[^1][^3]. One bulk transfer may pay several invoices at once, a one-to-many match[^32].
example.output: Matched pairs, each showing how it was matched and how confident the tool is[^3][^5]. An exception list with a suggested reason for each, such as a timing difference or a possible duplicate[^6]. A drafted explanation for each exception, which the reviewer checks before sign-off[^9].

recipes.name: 1. Small team on QuickBooks or Xero, one entity
recipes.when: Pick this for one entity and modest bank volume. The ledger's own AI reconcile is in your plan or a small add-on[^37][^38].
flow: Staff accountant: turn on the built-in AI reconcile for each bank account
Staff accountant: review the auto-reconciled list, which shows whether a rule, match, memory or prediction made each one
Staff accountant: clear the suggestions the tool was unsure about
Controller: sample auto-matched lines, then review and sign the reconciliation
recipes.cost: Xero Growing is $59 a month and QuickBooks Plus is $140 a month at list, read 26 Nov 2026[^37][^38]. Xero sells auto-reconcile as a $5 monthly add-on on its Early plan[^37].

recipes.name: 2. Mid-size firm on NetSuite or Sage Intacct, several entities
recipes.when: Pick this for several entities, many accounts and an audit that tests your controls. Close platforms add matching, task lists and audit trails[^27][^30].
flow: Controller: choose the accounts in scope and write match rules and tolerances (how far two amounts may differ and still match)
IT: connect the ERP and bank feeds, and own user access and change control
Controller: pilot one entity's bank accounts for two or three closes before adding the rest
Staff accountants: work the exception queue, accepting AI suggestions only above a tested confidence level
Auditor: review the match logs and IT controls
recipes.cost: Close platforms are quote-only[^27][^28]. Quotes scale with transactions and seats, close scope, or modules and users plus a one-time implementation fee[^28][^30][^36].

recipes.name: 3. Light build on tools you already own
recipes.when: Pick this when your matching rules are unusual and volume is low. Keep matching in fixed rules you can test, since your auditor must be able to rely on the data[^12][^9].
flow: Staff accountant: standardize reconciliation templates and import data with Power Query
Finance systems lead: write the matching rules as a script, not a prompt
Staff accountant: have an AI assistant draft explanations for exceptions only
Controller: approve every draft and keep the log
recipes.cost: Microsoft 365 Copilot Business is $21 per user a month, read 26 Nov 2026[^24]. ChatGPT Business is $20 per user a month billed yearly[^25].

rules.name: SOX 404 and PCAOB AS 2201
rules.what: Public companies have their internal controls over financial reporting audited, and reconciliation review is one of those controls[^13][^8]. Late or failed reviews show up as material weaknesses in 10-Ks and SEC orders[^8][^7][^15]. SOX 404 covers public companies; private-company audits follow AICPA standards instead[^13][^10].

rules.name: PCAOB AS 1105 and AS 2301 amendments (technology-assisted analysis)
rules.status: In force for audits of fiscal years starting on or after 15 Dec 2025
rules.what: Auditors must check that the electronic data you give them is reliable, with more weight on IT controls[^12][^11]. The rules are not AI-specific; they cover electronic information in general[^12]. Calendar-2026 audits are the first under them[^11].

rules.name: AICPA practice aid: AI Considerations for Financial Statement Auditors
rules.what: A 51-page guide on how a client's AI affects financial reporting and controls[^9][^10]. It is not binding. Private-company audits follow AICPA standards, so expect your auditor to know it[^10].

howToTest: Start with one process, such as bank reconciliations, and record today's days to close, hours per reconciliation and corrections after close[^16]. Note calendar or business days, since benchmarks use both[^16][^17].
Pilot on one entity or a few bank accounts first. Run the tool in parallel for two or three closes on prior months and compare it with the signed-off manual reconciliations.
Measure the auto-match rate, then sample auto-matched lines by the reason the tool records for each[^5][^6]. Check that each pair is the same transaction, not just the same amount.
Count both kinds of error: false matches and missed exceptions.
Check completeness: every bank and ledger line entered the run, and opening balances agree with last month's closing balances[^2][^1].
Log the method, confidence, software version and human action for every match[^3][^5].
Price the lift: hours freed times your loaded staff cost, plus days cut from the close. Compare your days to close with APQC's median of 6[^16].
watchOuts: Right total, wrong pairing: amounts can tie while the transactions are unrelated. Sample matches by the reason the tool records, not just the total[^5][^6].
Over-trusting suggestions: Xero auto-reconciles only when highly confident[^4]. Set your own auto-accept level from testing, and review everything below it[^3].
Made-up explanations: AICPA names hallucinations and explainability as AI risks[^9]. Treat AI-written causes as drafts a person verifies[^9].

Missing audit trail: CalCPA reports PCAOB findings where AI anomaly tools lacked documented calibration[^14]. Fewer than half of large finance teams say they can produce AI audit evidence without disruption[^20].
Weak controls get faster, not better: AI does not fix a review step that already fails. Reconciliation review failures already drive material weaknesses, so fix review first[^8][^7].

Bank data leaving the building: Intuit's privacy terms let it train AI on customer data and let people process what its AI assistants receive[^26]. Read your vendor's data terms before uploading bank files[^26].

faq.q: Do companies actually use AI for bank reconciliations?
faq.a: Yes, mostly through features built into the ledger[^6][^4]. QuickBooks and Xero suggest or confirm matches and leave unsure ones for a person[^6][^4].

faq.q: Will reconciliation software actually make the work faster?
faq.a: Often, if your data and review steps are in order. Ventana found 57% of firms with automated reconciliations closed within six business days, against 27% without[^17]. In Gartner's survey, 91% of finance teams saw only low or moderate AI impact at first, so plan for a ramp[^19].

faq.q: My company wants our reconciliation rebuilt in AI. Should it be?
faq.a: Keep the matching in fixed rules that give the same answer every run, and use AI to draft explanations. Your auditor must be able to rely on the data, and AICPA flags unexplainable AI output as a risk[^12][^9].

faq.q: Will our auditor accept AI-matched reconciliations?
faq.a: Yes, if the controls hold: a named preparer and reviewer, split duties, tested thresholds and a log for every match[^2][^1]. New PCAOB rules have auditors check how reliable your electronic data is[^12][^11].

faq.q: How much does account reconciliation software cost?
faq.a: Small-business ledgers with AI reconcile list at $27 to $340 a month[^37][^38]. Dedicated close platforms quote on request, scaled by transactions, seats or close scope[^28][^30]. Oracle's EPM suite lists $250 per named user a month, with a 10-user minimum[^23].

faq.q: Can AI handle one payment that covers many invoices?
faq.a: Some tools can: Trintech says its Adra matcher handles one-to-many and many-to-one matches[^32]. Workday's AI suggests matches for lines its rules left, with a confidence level a person reviews[^3]. Test your own hard cases in the pilot before you buy.

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy when your process is standard and you have no systems team. Firms now buy 76% of their AI use cases, up from 53% in 2024[^21]. MIT research found internal builds succeed about one-third as often as bought tools[^22].
buyVsBuild.build: Build a light layer when matching rules are unusual, such as processor formats or one payment for many invoices, and volume is low. Keep matching in fixed, testable rules and let AI draft explanations only, since AICPA flags unexplainable output as a risk[^9].

pickElse: Low volume and few accounts: use your ledger's own reconcile screen and bank rules in QuickBooks or Xero[^6][^4].
The real problem is upstream data: Gartner and KPMG both find data quality is the top barrier to AI in finance[^19][^20]. Fix integration and process first.
You need consolidation or a new ERP, not matching: look at a suite such as Oracle EPM or your ERP's own reconciliation module[^23][^36].
Messy multi-system matching with fixed rules: a Python or Power Query script gives the same answer every run, which is easier to test and audit[^12].

offer.heading: Stuck on month-end reconciliations? Get a free 30-minute diagnostic
offer.body: Walk us through your close and the accounts that eat the most time. You leave knowing where AI can match safely, what your auditor will want to see, and whether your built-in tools are enough. No sales pitch.

reviews.notes: Wanted a first process to fix and a before-and-after measure up front. The test section now opens by naming bank reconciliations as the starting point and the three numbers to record.
Flagged jargon a non-accountant would stall on: tolerances, deterministic, flux, 10-K filers. Each is now defined or swapped for plain words.
Asked whether one unit can try this before a company-wide rollout. Added a one-entity pilot to the test steps and to the mid-size build's flow.

The controller of a private firm could not tell whether SOX applied, and saw vendor studies cited as neutral. The SOX rule now says it covers public companies and points private firms to AICPA standards; vendor surveys and forum posts are cut in favor of GAO, Gartner and KPMG.

Steve wanted the small-firm tools named first and a plainer promise for the 30 minutes, with no pitch. The bottom line now leads with QuickBooks and Xero, and the offer says what he leaves with and that there is no sales pitch.
